concept.name: Liquidation cascade
concept.definition: A liquidation cascade is a self-reinforcing chain of forced position closures: falling prices trigger liquidations whose forced market sells push prices lower still, triggering the next tier of liquidations in rapid succession.
concept.intuition: It is an avalanche on a leveraged mountainside: each margin call knocks loose more snow, and the falling snow triggers the margin calls below.
concept.mechanics: Leveraged positions have liquidation prices set by maintenance margin (or health factors in DeFi); when price crosses a dense cluster of them, engines and liquidators market-sell collateral/positions into the book, deepening the move and hitting the next cluster. Open interest collapses, funding and basis gap, and thin order books amplify each leg — visible in Coin Metrics-style analyses combining OI, funding and liquidation data.
concept.failure_modes: Cascades overshoot any fundamental value — price can wick far below fair levels before recovering (the 'liquidation hunt' zone); exchange risk systems (ADL, insurance funds) socialize residual losses when liquidations cannot fill in time.
concept.misconceptions: Cascades are not proof of manipulation — they are the mechanical consequence of stacked leverage at similar levels, though actors can deliberately push price toward liquidation clusters ('stop hunting'). High leverage in a market is the fuel; any spark works.
concept.example: BTC drops 3% to $97,000 where a dense band of 25x longs liquidates; their forced selling drives $94,000, liquidating 10x longs, then $90,000 — billions in open interest wiped in an hour before buyers absorb the flow.

citations.source: Binance Support - Leverage and Margin of USD-M Futures
